question: Should experimental Claw manifests be allowed to create or reuse globally shared MCP declarations, and what host broker and authorization boundary is required before that capability can land?
rationale: The answer determines whether this belongs in core at all and, if it does, whether global names, executable commands, remote endpoints, and environment inheritance require brokered or namespaced handling; this cannot be selected safely by a mechanical repair.

options.title: Pause pending the RFC decision
options.body: Keep this stacked slice open but do not merge it until the RFC defines the canonical core-versus-plugin ownership and security boundary.

options.title: Approve a constrained core model
options.body: Sponsor core ownership only with brokered or allowlisted execution, explicit host authorization for reuse, narrow environment inheritance, and real upgrade/lifecycle proof.

options.title: Externalize MCP ownership
options.body: Move MCP declaration packaging and lifecycle authority to an approved plugin or bundle path rather than adding a second core ownership ledger.

recommendation.title: Pause pending the RFC decision
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked slice open but do not merge it until the RFC defines the canonical core-versus-plugin ownership and security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared MCP configuration surface is the current-main boundary this PR extends, and prior history ties that surface to Vincent Koc.
